title: The sacred cow raises a force
introduction: The seizure of Kaamadhenu, the Sacred Cow, causes anxiety in her and she urges Vashishta to counteract the atrocity of Vishvamitra. Agreeing to her, the sage asks the Cow to create a force that can subdue the forces of Vishvamitra. Accordingly, that Cow generates newer forces and a war ensues.
closing: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुःपंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 54th chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
कामधेनुं वसिष्ठोऽपि यदा न त्यजते मुनिः |
तदास्य शबलां राम विश्वामित्रोऽन्वकर्षत
verses.iast:
kāmadhenum vasiṣṭho api yadā na tyajate muniḥ |
tadā asya śabalām rāma viśvāmitro anvakarṣata
verses.translation: "When Sage Vashishta did not yield Kaamadhenu, the milker of any desire, oh, Rama, then Vishvamitra started to seize it." Sage Shataananda continued the narration of the legend of Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: Vishvamitra, that, Shabala, dragged - started to seize.

verses.devanagari:
नीयमाना तु शबला राम राज्ञा महात्मना |
दुःखिता चिन्तयामास रुदंती शोककर्षिता
verses.iast:
nīyamānā tu śabalā rāma rājñā mahātmanā |
duḥkhitā cintayāmāsa rudantī śoka karśitā
verses.translation: "While the determined king Vishvamitra dragged her away from Vashishta, oh, Rama, Shabala is saddened and tearfully mulled over stung by the anguish of her secession from the sage.

glosses.meaning: being led away - dragged her away

verses.devanagari:
परित्यक्ता वसिष्ठेन किमहं सुमहात्मना |
याहं राजभृतैर्दीना ह्रियेयं भृशदुःखिता
verses.iast:
parityaktā vasiṣṭhena kim aham sumahātmanā |
yā aham rāja bhṛtaiḥ dīnā hriyeyam bhṛśa duḥkhitā
verses.translation: " 'A pitiable and highly anguished one, such as I am. I am being dragged away by the servants of the king. Has this great souled Sage Vashishta abandoned me, or what?

glosses.meaning: which, me - such as I am
who am stolen - being led away

verses.devanagari:
किं मयापकृतं तस्य महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः |
यन्मामनागसं भक्तामिष्टां त्यजति धार्मिकः
verses.iast:
kim mayā apakṛtam tasya maharṣeḥ bhāvita ātmanaḥ |
yan mām anāgasam bhaktām iṣṭām tyajati dhārmikaḥ
verses.translation: " 'Or, did I do any misdeed towards that great sage of sacred soul whereby he is leaving me off. I have always been reverent and a cherished cow to that pietist and am I no errant.' That cow eulogised in this manner.

verses.devanagari:
इति संचिन्तयित्वा तु निःश्वस्य च पुनः पुनः |
जगाम वेगेन तदा वसिष्ठं परमौजसम्
निर्धूय तां तदा भृत्यान् शतशः शत्रुसूदन |
जगामानिलवेगेन पादमूलं महात्मनः
verses.iast:
iti sañcintayitvā tu niḥśvasya ca punaḥ punaḥ |
jagāma vegena tadā vasiṣṭham parama ojasam
nirdhūya tām tadā bhṛtyān śataśaḥ śatrusūdana |
jagāma anila vegena pāda mūlam mahātmanaḥ
verses.translation: "On thinking thus and suspiring repeatedly, oh, enemy-subjugator, Rama, then she that Sacred Cow hastily rushed with the speed a gust and went to that highly energetic Vashishta on utterly shoving off hundreds of attendants of the king who are roping her, and then she straight went to the base of the feet of the great-souled Vashishta.

glosses.meaning: thenl anila vegena = gust, with speed of
towards highly energetic one, to Vashishta
to foot, base, she went to.

verses.devanagari:
शबला सा रुदन्ती च क्रोशन्ती चेदमब्रवीत् |
वसिष्ठस्याग्रतः स्थित्वा मेघदुन्दुभिनिःस्वना
verses.iast:
śabalā sā rudantī ca krośantī ca idam abravīt |
vasiṣṭhasya agrataḥ sthitvā megha niḥsvanā
verses.translation: "She that moaning and groaning Shabala staying before the Sage Vashishta spoke this bellowing like a thunderous cloud.

glosses.meaning: cloud, with bellows - bellowing like thunder of the cloud

verses.devanagari:
भगवन् किं परित्यक्ता त्वयाहं ब्रह्मणः सुत |
यस्माद्राजभटा मां हि नयन्ते त्वत्सकाशतः
verses.iast:
bhagavan kim parityaktā tvayā aham brahmaṇaḥ suta |
yasmāt rāja bhaṭā mām hi nayante tvat sakāśataḥ
verses.translation: " 'Oh, Son of Brahma, why I am discarded by you, whereby oh, god, the king's attendants are weaning me away from your proximity.' So Shabala urged Vashishta.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु ब्रह्मर्षिरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् |
शोकसंतप्तहृदयां स्वसारमिव दुःखिताम्
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ tu brahmarṣir idam vacanam abravīt |
śoka santapta hṛdayām sva sāram iva duḥkhitām
verses.translation: "When he is spoken thus, then that Brahma-sage spoke this sentence to worrisome Shabala, whose heart is worrying with worry, as he would speak with his own sister in her worriment.

glosses.meaning: thus, spoke to, on his part, Brahma-sage
by worry, worrying, hearted [to worrisome Shabala]
worried, to his own, sister, as with

verses.devanagari:
न त्वां त्यजामि शबले नापि मेऽपकृतं त्वया |
एष त्वां नयते राजा बलान्मत्तो महाबलः
verses.iast:
na tvām tyajāmi śabale na api me apakṛtam tvayā |
eṣa tvām nayate rājā balāt mat.htaḥ mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: " 'Neither I forswear you nor you fouled me, oh, Shabala, this king is forcibly weaning you away from me as he is beside himself with kingly arrogance.

glosses.meaning: by you, to me, not, misdeed done, even - you too have not fouled me
ecstatic by his own might - king]

verses.devanagari:
न हि तुल्यं बलं मह्यं राजा त्वद्य विशेषतः |
बली राजा क्षत्रियश्च पृथिव्याः पतिरेव च
verses.iast:
na hi tulyam balam mahyam rājā tu adya viśeṣataḥ |
balī rājā kṣatriyaḥ ca pṛthivyāḥ patiḥ eva ca
verses.translation: " 'My ability is not balanceable with his, isn't it. Above all, on his part he is a king now, and a king will be mighty, he is the lord of the land and a Kshatriya, and thus we have to be subservient to a Kshatriya, isn't it.

glosses.meaning: [he is a] king, on his part

verses.devanagari:
इयमक्षौहिणी पूर्णा गजवाजिरथाकुला |
हस्तिध्वजसमाकीर्णा तेनासौ बलवत्तरः
verses.iast:
iyam akṣauhiṇī pūrṇā gaja vāji ratha ākulā |
hasti dhvaja samākīrṇā tena asau balavattaraḥ
verses.translation: " 'This akshauhini unit of army is plethoric, overcrowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, and overspread with flags and elephants, thereby he is mightier than me.' Thus Vashishta tried to pacify that Sacred-Cow.

glosses.meaning: he is, in might, higher in degree - mightier than me.

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्ता वसिष्ठेन प्रत्युवाच विनीतवत् |
वचनं वचनज्ञा सा ब्रह्मर्षिमतुलप्रभम्
verses.iast:
evam uktā vasiṣṭhena pratyuvāca vinītavat |
vacanam vacanajñā sā brahmarṣim atula prabham
verses.translation: "She who is spoken that way by Vashishta, that sententious Sacred Cow, Shabala, in her turn obediently spoke this sentence to that Brahma-sage of un-balanceable resplendence.

glosses.meaning: by Vashishta, that way, spoken [to Cow]
to the one with un-balanceable, resplendence

verses.devanagari:
न बलं क्षत्रियस्याहुर्ब्राह्मणो बलवत्तरः |
ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मबलं दिव्यं क्षत्रात्तु बलवत्तरम्
verses.iast:
na balam kṣatriyasya āhuḥ brāhmaṇo balavattaraḥ |
brahman brahma balam divyam kṣatrāt tu balavattaram
verses.translation: " 'Oh, Brahman, unstated is that the might of sovereignty as mightier than the might of sagacity. A sage is mightier than a sovereign. A sage's might is mightiest than the mightier sovereign, for a sage's might is angelic.' So Shabala started talking to the sage.
notes: This is the relevant stanza for the later time debates or essay competitions under the caption of 'pen vs. sword... which is mightier...' Here, though Vishvamitra is well aware that a sage's possession cannot be usurped, he resorted to the same. The Sacred Cow is telling the above with intolerance towards Vishvamitra's violation of the norms. sā api asahamānā kāma dohinī śāntyā kṣamayā yuktam vaśiṣṭam avocat -

What a king has got to do with a sage's wealth? A sage acquires it with his ascesis and it is not another king's kingdom to conquer. sarva dhamajñasyā api viśvāmitrasya etādṛśī buddhiḥ abūt | yasmai devā prayaccanti puruṣāya parābhavam - bala avalepana viśvamitro vaśiṣṭha vākyam anādṛtya brahmasva hareṇa mahā doṣam jānan api balāt eva śabalām ācakarṣa - dk The scriptures, norms, ethics demand that a sagacious person shall not be robbed off his possession, which he acquires by his personal merit. But Vishvamitra's brain tilted this way because of his all-conquering avarice and he thought that this cow is also conquerable, and gods give such a mind only to see the greedy to fail and thus insulted of their might.

na tu eva kadācit svayam rājā brahmaṇasva adadīta - bodhāyana sūtra - atha api udāharanti - na viṣam viṣam iti āhuḥ brahmasvam viṣam ucya te | brahmasvam putra pautra ghnam viṣam ekākinam haret | 'a sagacious person's possession is not to be snatched away - bodhāyana sūtrā-s; 'a poison if consumed kills one that consumes it... but the possession of a sagacious person, if tried for consumption, it consumes whole lot of the consumer's sons, grandsons and his clan itself, besides the consumer...for sage's possession in itself is a lethal poison...'

glosses.meaning: not, speak of [unstated as 'balavat taraH' mighty, more = mightier than a Brahman's, i.e., than the might of a sage]

verses.devanagari:
अप्रमेयबलं तुभ्यं न त्वया बलवत्तरः |
विश्वामित्रो महावीर्यस्तेजस्तव दुरासदम्
verses.iast:
aprameya balam tubhyam na tvayā balavattaraḥ |
viśvāmitro mahāvīryaḥ tejaḥ tava durāsadam
verses.translation: " 'Immutable is your power as you are mightier than great-mighty Vishvamitra and invincible is your dynamism.

glosses.meaning: mighty, more than - mightier than you

verses.devanagari:
नियुङ्क्ष्व मां महातेजस्त्वद्ब्रह्मबलसंभृताम् |
तस्य दर्पं बलं यत्नं नाशयामि दुरात्मनः
verses.iast:
niyuñkṣva mām mahātejaḥ tvat brahma bala sambhṛtām |
tasya darpam balam yat.hnam nāśayāmi durātmanaḥ
verses.translation: " 'Ordain me, oh, highly resplendent sage, who am replete with the power of your sagacity, and I will disprove the vanity, valour, and venture of that injudicious king for this injudicious seizure.' Thus Shabala implored the sage Vashishta.

glosses.meaning: with your, Brahma's [sagacity's] power, replete with [i.e., me]
his [Vishvamitra's,] vanity, valour, venture [to wean me from you]

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्तस्तु तया राम वसिष्ठः सुमहायशाः |
सृजस्वेति तदोवाच बलं परबलार्दनम्
verses.iast:
iti uktaḥ tu tayā rāma vasiṣṭhaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ |
sṛjasva iti tadā uvāca balam para bala ardanam
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, when spoken by her thus, that highly glorious Vashishta said to Shabala, the do-all cow, 'create a power that can overpower the power of opponent.' Vashishta said so to Shabala.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सुरभिः सा असृजत्तदा |
तस्या हुंभारवोत्सृष्टाः पह्लवाः शतशो नृप
नाशयन्ति बलं सर्वं विश्वामित्रस्य पश्यतः |
verses.iast:
tasya tat vacanam śrutvā surabhiḥ sā asṛjat tadā |
tasyā humbhā rava ut.hsṛṣṭāḥ pahlavāḥ śataśo nṛpa
nāśayanti balam sarvam viśvāmitrasya paśyataḥ |
verses.translation: "On hearing his sentence, oh, Rama, that Sacred Cow Shabala then created Pahlava kings, sprang forth from her mooing 'hums', and hundreds of them annihilated the army of Vishvamitra in its entirety just while Vishvamitra is witnessing it.

verses.devanagari:
स राजा परमक्रुद्धः क्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः
पह्लवान्नाशयामास शस्त्रैरुच्चावचैरपि |
verses.iast:
sa rājā parama kruddhaḥ krodha visphārita īkṣaṇaḥ
pahlavān nāśayāmāsa śastraiḥ uccāvacaiḥ api |
verses.translation: "King Vishvamitra was utterly infuriated and with wide-eyed anger he started to destroy those Pahlava-s with many a kind of his weaponry.

verses.devanagari:
विश्वामित्रार्दितान् दृष्ट्वा पह्लवान् शतशस्तदा
भूय एवासृजद्घोरान् शकान् यवनमिश्रितान् |
verses.iast:
viśvāmitra arditān dṛṣṭvā pahlavān śataśaḥ tadā
bhūya eva asṛjat ghorān śakān yavana miśritān |
verses.translation: "On seeing the subdual of hundreds of Pahlava-s by Vishvamitra, then the Sacred Cow again generated deadly Shaka-s hobnobbed with Yavana-s through her mooing 'hums'.
notes: These Shaka-s and Yavana-s are the Shakas, or the Scythians, or the Indo-Scythians of Max Muller. Some discussion about this is included in the endnote of Kishkindha, Ch. 43. Dharmaakuutam says: tadanu vaśiṣṭha abhyanujñātā śabalā nirmita pahlava ādi - nikṛṣṭa jāti - niṣūditam svam balam viśvāmitra - iti - dk These are viewed as deadly, lowly, ruffian class of warriors in Indian viewpoint and created out of thin air by this Sacred Cow.

verses.devanagari:
तैरासीत् संवृता भूमिः शकैर्यवनमिश्रितैः
प्रभावद्भिर्महावीर्यैर्हेमकिंजल्कसंनिभैः |
verses.iast:
taiḥ āsīt saṃvṛtā bhūmiḥ śakaiḥ yavana miśritaiḥ
prabhāvadbhirmahāvīryairhemakiñjalkasannibhaiḥ | - yadvā -
prabhāvadbhiḥ mahāvīryaiḥ hema kiñjalka saṃnibhaiḥ |
verses.translation: "Then the earth was pervaded with the Shaka-s associated with Yavana-s, who have effectuation and bravery in overcoming their enemy forces, and who are golden in bodily colour similar to the golden pistils of flowers which complexion is outlandish.

glosses.meaning: those that are golden, pistils, similar to

verses.devanagari:
दीर्घासिपट्टिशधरैर्हेमवर्णाम्बरावृतैः
निर्दग्धं तद्बलं सर्वं प्रदीप्तैरिव पावकैः |
verses.iast:
dīrghāsipaṭṭiśadharairhemavarṇāmbarāavṛtaiḥ || - yadvā -
dīrgha asi paṭṭiśa dharaiḥ hema varṇa ambara āvṛtaiḥ
nir.hdagdham tat balam sarvam pradīptaiḥ iva pāvakaiḥ |
verses.translation: "Yavana-s and Shaka-s, who are wielding bowie knives and broad lances and who are clad in golden coloured dresses, and who looked like glowing fires have completely burnt down entire force of Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: who are - glowing, fires, as with

verses.devanagari:
ततोऽस्त्राणि महातेजा विश्वामित्रो मुमोच ह |
तैस्तैर्यवनकांभोजा बर्बराश्चाकुलीकृताः
verses.iast:
tato astrāṇi mahātejā viśvāmitro mumoca ha |
taiḥ taiḥ yavana kāmbhojā barbarāḥ ca akulī kṛtāḥ
verses.translation: "Then that great-resplendent Vishvamitra indeed released his missiles, by which Yavana-s, Kaambhoja-s, and the Barbara-s, are rendered helter-skelter." Thus Sage Shataananda continued his narration of Vishvamitra. [1-54-23b,c.]
notes: The Barbara-s are said in this text whereas other mms contain it as "Pahlava-s'. Even on taking Barbara-s, they are an outlandish clan and the word 'Barbara' might have been the ancestor word of the present day 'Barbarian.'
